instructions.task: Assign this claim about an English expression to one construction id from the criteria.
instructions.rules:
Assignment rules (they align this task with an existing keyed extraction):
- subject, object, complement of a preposition, 'independent use', pro-form or anaphoric use, NP use without a following nominal -> independent_argument. A relative-clause postmodifier on such a phrase does not change this.
- an independent phrase with a partitive of-PP -> independent_partitive.
- Det or determiner before a separate nominal (the book, few doctors, some teachers) -> dependent_det. Internal Mod / attributive position before a separate nominal (numerous people, the rich man) -> dependent_internal_mod.
- a degree adverb attached INSIDE the phrase (very few, so many, too much, how little, as few as, quite a few) -> internal_mod_admission. An adjective inside the phrase (the lucky few, poor old me, lucky you) -> internal_mod_admission.
- an approximative or focusing adverb attached OUTSIDE (almost every, nearly all, hardly any, practically no, only you, absolutely nothing) -> peripheral_mod_admission.
- the phrase itself modifies an adjective (a great deal better, enough good, plenty big, two years old) -> degree_modifier_adj; the phrase modifies a verb, adverb, preposition, determinative or comparative (I hadn't prepared enough, this big, a lot more) -> degree_modifier_nonadj.
- predicative complement of a copula (they are many, that is mine) -> predicative_complement; than-phrase -> comparative_complement; existential there -> existential_displaced_subject.
- if the sentence is about the analysis of the phrase (ordinary Head, fusion, ultimate lexical head, constraint fragment rows that only restate a permission) choose the construction the permission concerns, not fused_head, unless fusion itself is the point.
- Use taxonomic_or_meta only when no construction is at issue. Use other only when nothing fits, and say what in other_label.

criteria.dependent_det: A phrase functions as Det before a separate target nominal.
criteria.dependent_internal_mod: A phrase functions as internal Mod before a separate target nominal.
criteria.independent_argument: A phrase has an ordinary subject, object, or preposition-complement use without a separate target nominal.
criteria.independent_partitive: An independent phrase contains a partitive of-PP.
criteria.degree_modifier_adj: A phrase functions as a degree modifier of an adjective.
criteria.existential_displaced_subject: A phrase functions as displaced subject in an existential there-construction, with dummy there as subject.
criteria.internal_mod_admission: A phrase admits a modifier attached inside its own nominal projection; the query states the modifier and its position.
criteria.peripheral_mod_admission: A phrase admits a peripheral modifier attached outside its own determiner and internal nominal dependents; the query states the modifier.
criteria.comparative_complement: A phrase contains a comparative than-phrase complement.
criteria.degree_modifier_nonadj: A phrase functions as a degree modifier of a non-adjectival target; the query states the target category.
criteria.predicative_complement: A phrase functions as predicative complement of a copular verb.
criteria.genitive_marking: The phrase takes genitive marking or has a genitive form (Kim's, my/mine, whose).
criteria.number_agreement: The phrase controls or transmits subject-verb agreement or number (number transparency, singular/plural selection).
criteria.number_inflection: The phrase inflects for number (plural -s) or lacks a number contrast.
criteria.grade_inflection: The phrase has comparative or superlative inflection or a grade paradigm (fewer/fewest, more/most, less/least).
criteria.predeterminer_mod: The phrase functions as predeterminer modifier before a determined NP (all the books, both these).
criteria.coordination_marker: The phrase functions as a marker of coordination (both ... and, either ... or, neither ... nor).
criteria.compound_base: The phrase is the determinative base of a compound (anyone, something, nothing) or the claim concerns a compound's modifier domain.
criteria.fused_head: The claim concerns the fused-head analysis (fused determiner-head or modifier-head) of the phrase, or an ordinary-Head versus fusion comparison.
criteria.external_determination: The phrase, itself determinative-headed, takes an external determiner (the few, the lucky few, a certain, the very few).
criteria.taxonomic_or_meta: The sentence makes a taxonomic, analytical, or methodological statement about a category or class, not a claim about a specific construction.
criteria.other: None of the above. Give other_label in a few words.

evidence_type.instructions: What basis does the manuscript sentence give for this claim? Classify the stated grounds, not their strength.

criteria.cgel_described: the sentence reports a description or analysis from CGEL (Huddleston & Pullum 2002), usually with a citation
criteria.cgel_restricted: the sentence reports a restriction or exclusion stated in CGEL
criteria.other_source_described: the sentence reports a description from a source other than CGEL (Payne, Hudson, Spinillo, Lyons, Sommerstein, Palmer, Reynolds' earlier papers)
criteria.constructed_illustration: the basis is a constructed example presented as possible or well formed
criteria.constructed_ungrammatical: the basis is a constructed example marked ungrammatical or excluded
criteria.retained_attestation: the basis is an attested corpus or web example, usually with a footnoted source
criteria.searched_not_found: the sentence reports a search that returned no qualifying attestation
criteria.authors_analysis: the sentence states the manuscript's own analysis or proposal, not a source or an example
criteria.not_determinable: the basis cannot be determined from the sentence
